content.comment_body: Hello, I am using five analog inputs—four on the main [product_name] unit. I added an analog module to handle a fifth input. When I check the analog channels, the module shows a small input value even with nothing connected. As a result, the display doesn't show zero; this issue occurs for both module inputs. The four main inputs work correctly. I can apply a -0.03 offset to achieve a zero reading, but that affects measurements during operation. Is there a configuration setting I’m missing? Best regards, [user_name]
No, analog inputs have defined error tolerances. For the main module, this is about ±1.5%, roughly ±0.15 V. The same applies to the added expansion module.

Hi, sorry for my late response and thanks for your answer. If the expansion module has the same specifications as the main unit, why does the base always read zero when no input is connected, but the expansion module registers a value—such as a speed of 3 min when the maximum is set to 300—even with nothing connected? If that's the case, these expansion modules aren’t suitable when a true zero reading is needed; does that mean a base voltage or current is always present?
Having equal error tolerance does not guarantee identical performance across all inputs. Some may exhibit this behavior, while others might not.

analysis.insight_summary: The user notes that analog expansion modules for [product_name] report non-zero values even with no connected sensor, in contrast to the main unit’s inputs. This creates challenges in applications where a true zero is required, leading to concerns about hardware consistency and the effectiveness of applying offsets. Error tolerance specifications are discussed, but uncertainty remains about input accuracy.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the analog input of the expansion module to display exactly zero when there is no connected signal, matching the behavior of the base unit. User looks for configuration settings or options to correct or offset readings without compromising measurement accuracy.
